transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately I just can’t think clearly or make decisions the way I used to, and it’s starting to affect my work and plans. I'm a truck driver, and this constant fog is making it hard to focus on the road or figure out how to move forward.
Along with this brain fog, do you often feel extremely tired during the day, or has anyone told you that you snore loudly or gasp for air while sleeping?
I definitely feel completely wiped out and drained during the day, starting from the moment I wake up. As for snoring or gasping for air, I really don't know since I live alone.
Have you also been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, or have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, most days it feels like there's a gray cloud sitting on me, leaving me feeling empty and pointless. Nothing feels enjoyable anymore, even when I'm off the clock, so I've mostly stopped showing up to softball and volunteering and just go through the motions.
Since you live alone and aren't sure about snoring, do you ever wake up gasping for breath, or notice that you regularly have a dry mouth or a headache first thing in the morning?
No, I don't recall ever waking up gasping for breath. I also haven't really noticed having a dry mouth or any headaches when I get up in the morning.
Have you recently experienced any head injuries, or do you have any diagnosed medical conditions, such as thyroid or neurological issues?
No, I haven't had any head injuries or anything like that. I also don't have any diagnosed medical conditions, so my thyroid and neurological health should be fine as far as I know.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of low mood, emptiness, and loss of interest in your activities?

Looking back, this low, drained way of feeling has been my normal for about three years now. It really seemed to start when my work schedule shifted from mostly local runs to those irregular long-haul routes.
During these past three years, have you had any periods lasting longer than two months where your mood returned to normal and you felt like your usual self?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling normal that lasted anywhere near that long. Since the schedule change three years ago, this low, drained, and foggy feeling has just been my constant state without any real breaks. At most, I might get a couple of days of slight relief, but then it's right back to this gray cloud.
Along with the low mood, have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts of death or suicide?

I definitely struggle with feeling worthless, constantly telling myself I'm just a washed-up truck driver who screws everything up and isn't meant to get ahead. However, I don't have any thoughts of death or suicide; it's just a lot of self-blame and feeling like a failure.
How has your sleep or your appetite been since these feelings started three years ago?

My sleep is pretty awful—I lie awake for over an hour with my mind spinning about work, and then I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning unable to drift back to sleep, leaving me completely exhausted. My appetite hasn't really changed much though, so that isn't a major issue for me.
When this gray cloud first started three years ago, did it hit you suddenly and severely all at once, or did it develop as a milder, gradual low mood that slowly became your normal?

It was definitely a gradual, slow-creeping process rather than a sudden crash. When my work routes changed three years ago, it slowly wore me down until this low, drained feeling just became my "new normal" that I blamed on getting older and working a tough job.

During these past three years, has the intensity of your low mood and fatigue remained at a steady, constant level, or did it ever become so severe that you were completely unable to work or function?

It has been a steady, constant drag rather than hitting me in sudden, disabling waves. I haven't been completely unable to work, but it drains me so much that I make more routing mistakes and have no energy left for anything besides driving and crashing on the couch.
Before these past three years, did you ever experience any other periods of depression or low mood, or has this been the very first time in your life you've felt this way?

Yes, this is the very first time in my life I've ever felt this way. Before three years ago, when I was still on local routes, I felt completely fine and was really active with softball, volunteering, and socializing. But once my schedule changed, this low, foggy feeling started and has just been constant ever since.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a chronic depressed mood ('gray cloud') that has been continuously present for three years, meeting the minimum two-year duration criterion for Dysthymia (F34.1). The onset was gradual and has remained a steady, constant drag rather than occurring in discrete, severe episodes. The patient has not had any symptom-free periods lasting longer than two months and exhibits multiple associated symptoms, including insomnia, fatigue, low self-esteem (worthlessness), and poor concentration/difficulty making decisions, which collectively support F34.1 over an acute depressive episode (F32).
